q: A website offers a carbon or green certificate for a fee. Is it worth buying?
title: Paid online green certificates
short: Usually not. A buyer or lender values numbers that can be traced to your bills, and a verification statement from an accredited body. A certificate issued after a short online form, with no evidence checked, proves little. Check who issues it and whether anyone looked at your data.

ul: Which standard does it follow, for example ISO 14064-1?
Is the issuer accredited to verify under ISO 14065?
Will they look at your bills and invoices, or only a form?
Will the result name your figures, boundary and period?

p: An inventory built from your own records, and if a buyer asks, a verification statement from an accredited verifier.

senseible: Senseible keeps each figure behind a claim traceable to the invoices and bills it came from, so a reader can check the number rather than take the wording on trust.
